results.title: Anovion still aiming for 2026 construction | The Post-Searchlight
results.content:
As Anovion’s main product is synthetic graphite, a key component in electric vehicles, federal policy decisions and bills have also had an impact on the company. The most recent influencing factors include the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, as well as tariffs. Donnelly stated that Anovion is still assessing the impacts of the OBBBA, with some positives and negatives for battery cell producers. One positive he pointed out was restrictions placed on the use of foreign entity of concern (FEOC) [...] “As 95%+ of synthetic graphite used for battery cells currently comes from China, there should be tailwinds for Anovion’s value proposition to domestic cell makers coming out of the OBBBA,” Donnelly said, “but the ongoing uncertainty around tariffs and trade policy also plays a significant role in timing of the project and contracts.” [...] “Anovion wants to get into business at scale in Bainbridge as fast as we prudently can to address both the national security needs of the US and build out a critical part of the battery supply chain of the energy transition throughout North America,” Donnelly concluded.
